claims.text: Submitted by Luis D. Elizondo, Director, National Programs Special Management Staff, OUSD(I), on 9 August 2017 and approved 24 August 2017, covering three .mpg files: GoFast, Gimbal and FLIR.

States the purpose as 'Not for publication. Research and analysis ONLY and info sharing with other USG and industry partners for the purposes of developing a database to help identify, analyze, and ultimately defeat UAS threats.'
The version originally published by George Knapp had Elizondo's name and DoD title redacted; the unredacted FOIA copy identifies him.

desc: A Department of Defense Clearance Request for Public Release of Department of Defense Information, submitted by Luis D. Elizondo in his capacity as Director, National Programs Special Management Staff, OUSD(I), on 9 August 2017 and approved on 24 August 2017. It covers three .mpg files named 'GoFast', 'Gimbal' and 'FLIR'. The stated purpose is precise and, read carefully, does not authorise publication: 'Not for publication. Research and analysis ONLY and info sharing with other USG and industry partners for the purposes of developing a database to help identify, analyze, and ultimately defeat UAS threats.' The subject matter is described in terms of UAV, balloons and other unmanned aircraft systems, with no reference to unidentified phenomena. This one form carries most of the weight in the dispute over how the videos entered the public record: it proves Elizondo processed the AATIP-associated imagery from inside OUSD(I) in August 2017, and it simultaneously undercuts the claim that the government cleared the footage for public release. The Navy's Joseph Gradisher later stated that neither the cognizant Navy offices nor DOPSR had any record of a request for unrestricted release in 2017.
